# Test-cache key ignores environment identity: canonical post-push verification can silently cache-serve (SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L)

## Problem statement

The per-repo test cache keys entries on command + git fingerprint (HEAD + dirty-path content, or the pushed tree SHA) only. A green full-suite run recorded **inside a worktree** whose runtime environment differs from the canonical checkout — an unpopulated submodule (observed on RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK: `core` failed to clone, 'transport file not allowed', populated manually), a symlinked `node_modules`, a different interpreter — is byte-identical in key to a canonical-checkout run of the same tree, and is deliberately mirrored into `<main>/.worklog/cache` by `.githooks/pre-push` (`mirror_suite_cache`, "an identical key is an identical run"). Post-push verification, the dev-push gate's cached reuse and the audit skill can therefore report a green verdict that never executed (or never executed correctly) in the environment the verdict claims to evidence. The environment-blind key silently violates the cache's own correctness guarantee: identical key does not imply identical runtime environment.

## Users

- **Build agents using the implement skill**: an agent finishing a work item trusts "full suite green" as evidence the pushed tree passes; today a worktree-recorded run can masquerade as canonical-checkout evidence.
- **Auditors/reviewers (audit skill F3/F4)**: read-only full-suite evidence must describe the canonical checkout's environment, not a drifted worktree.

User stories:

- As a build agent, I want the post-push verification to be green only when the pushed tree is provably green in the canonical environment (fresh run or provably equivalent-environment cached run), so a drifted worktree's run cannot silently satisfy my verification.
- As an auditor, I want a cached full-suite entry to carry the environment that produced it, so I can distinguish "run in the canonical environment at this tree" from "run in a differently-provisioned worktree".

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — After `implement.py finish` pushes from a worktree, a post-push verification for the canonical (main) checkout cannot be served a full-suite entry recorded in an environment that differs from the canonical environment (submodule completeness, `node_modules` resolution, interpreter). When no canonical-environment entry exists for the pushed tree, the post-push step escalates: it executes a forced run in the canonical checkout — `--scope changed --force` as the default for narrow changes, escalating to a forced full run (`--scope full --force`) when the change is broad, a refactor, or environment drift (missing submodule, `node_modules` divergence) is detected — and uses that run as the verdict.
- AC2 — A cache-servable invocation in the canonical checkout no longer returns green from an entry recorded in a differently-provisioned worktree without executing: the environment fingerprint part of the key makes such an entry a miss, so the run executes fresh (no silent cache-serve).
- AC3 — The per-repo test cache key captures a **coarse, path-independent environment fingerprint** — submodule checkout completeness (`git submodule status`), `node_modules` resolution state (symlink target / installed lockfile state), interpreter identity — folded into the fingerprint alongside the existing git/tree state. An in-worktree run and a main-checkout run for the same commit produce distinct entries when their environments differ, and **share** entries when their environments are equivalent (path-independent reuse preserved). The environment fingerprint is computed cheaply and deterministically at lookup and store time, in the consumer's own checkout.
- AC4 — Fast iteration is preserved: targeted forced changed-scope runs remain the default post-push escalation for narrow changes; the forced full suite runs only for broad/refactor changes or detected environment drift. Same-tree + equivalent-environment cross-checkout sharing continues to work unchanged.
- AC5 — Each entry records the environment fingerprint (and its component descriptor: submodule status, `node_modules` resolution, interpreter) as provenance metadata alongside `fingerprint_kind`/`interpreter`; the pre-push mirroring either skips entries whose environment fingerprint cannot be matched to the canonical environment or records them so consumers can reject them. Documented in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 9 and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (exact escalation commands, when a forced full run is required vs a targeted one), with audit skill F3/F4 notes where relevant.
- AC6 — Regression tests in `tests/` where the cache layer and gates are tested: (a) drift-keyed entries are never served to a canonical-environment consumer — the canonical lookup misses and executes; (b) equivalent-environment entries still share across checkouts (finish gate ↔ pre-push ↔ audit); (c) the escalation path runs `--scope changed --force` for narrow changes and `--scope full --force` on detected drift/refactor; (d) existing cache provenance tests stay green.
- AC7 — Validation and docs: at least one automated test exercises each changed code path above; all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, module docstrings, and any relevant wiki or docs entries; the full project test suite passes with the new changes (CHANGELOG.md excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline).

## Impact

Agents can trust that a green post-push verification was executed against (or provably recorded in) the canonical environment — a silently cache-served verdict from a differently-provisioned worktree can no longer masquerade as proof the shipped tree passes.

## Constraints

- Do not break the audit skill's read-only full-suite verification: the 2 h TTL caching and tree-keyed reuse stay functional for entries recorded in an environment equivalent to the querying checkout.
- **Coarse and path-independent** environment identity only (producer decision Q2a): never the git common dir or absolute worktree path — that would kill the cross-checkout reuse that SA-0MWAXZHOU000UBG1 and SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI (audit tree-keyed cache reuse, both open) rely on. Reconcile with those items rather than duplicate or block them.
- The environment fingerprint must be cheap (sub-second, no full `node_modules` tree hashing) and deterministic, so it does not add measurable overhead to the hot cache path and does not produce spurious misses on innocuous churn (npm reinstall touching mtimes without changing installed state).
- Do not break the pre-push gate's in-place worktree execution model (SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH): a fresh detached checkout has no dependencies, so the gate keeps measuring a clean checkout of the pushed commit; only the entry's bindability to canonical-environment evidence changes.
- Reconcile with SA-0MVCF5SHU002WNYU (document pre-push bypass + verification recipe) and SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG (live-repo guard) rather than duplicating.
- Escalation executes suites inside `finish`, which holds the exclusive main-checkout lock: keep the escalated run targeted by default (AC4) and route it through the existing paced/locked test runner when running in the main checkout; a dirty/locked main checkout must degrade to a documented recovery rather than a silent green.

## Existing state

- Post-push verification is read-only and tree-keyed: `_resolve_post_push_verification()` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` executes nothing; it queries the pushed commit's tree SHA (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`) in the worktree, then the main checkout (SA-0MVXUSED6008J04R; cross-check SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN). `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 9 has no bare `/skill:test` post-push step.
- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --gate-commit <sha>` (worktree in place by design), then `mirror_suite_cache()` copies entries into `<main>/.worklog/cache` assuming content-addressed identity (SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3).
- Cache key = normalized command + git fingerprint + scope/type namespace; `store()` metadata records only `interpreter` as environment provenance. Verified against `dev` HEAD: `skill/test_cache.py` (`compute_git_state`/`compute_tree_state`, `cache_key`, `lookup`/`store`), `.githooks/pre-push` `mirror_suite_cache`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` ("Cache keys stay path-independent… an identical key is an identical run").

## Desired change

1. Add a cheap, deterministic, **path-independent environment fingerprint** (submodule completeness via `git submodule status`, `node_modules` resolution state, interpreter identity) to `skill/test_cache.py`, folded into the cache fingerprint so store and lookup bind git/tree state + environment. Record the environment descriptor as provenance metadata in each entry.
2. Update `run_tests.py` and the gate/finish call sites to compute the environment fingerprint in the checkout they measure/query, so tree-keyed and worktree-keyed lookups include it.
3. Extend `_resolve_post_push_verification()` in `implement.py` with the producer-chosen escalation (Q3a): when no canonical-environment entry exists for the pushed tree, execute `--scope changed --force` in the canonical checkout (targeted default), escalating to a forced full run on broad/refactor/drift; the escalated run's verdict replaces the read-only miss.
4. Make `mirror_suite_cache` environment-aware: only mirror (or label) entries whose environment fingerprint matches the canonical checkout, so a drifted-worktree entry cannot be served by main-checkout consumers.
5. Document the exact commands and escalation policy in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 9, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, and audit F3/F4 notes; add regression tests (AC6).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test_cache.py` — environment fingerprint computation + folding into `compute_git_state`/`compute_tree_state`/`cache_key`/`lookup`/`store`; provenance metadata (submodule status, `node_modules` resolution, interpreter).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — env fingerprint for gate runs (`--gate-commit`) and cache lookup/store; `--scope/--force` escalation support.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_resolve_post_push_verification()` escalation to forced targeted/full run in the canonical checkout when no canonical-environment entry exists.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — `mirror_suite_cache` environment-awareness (skip or label drift-keyed entries).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Step 9 post-push escalation wording and exact commands.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — cache-compatibility and post-push verification documentation.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — F3/F4 notes on environment-provenance-aware evidence where needed.
- `tests/test_test_cache.py`, `tests/test_pre_push_*.py`, `tests/test_finish_*` (e.g. `test_pre_push_gate_reuse.py`) — regression tests for drift-miss, equivalent-env sharing, and escalation.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Environment-fingerprint instability** — npm reinstall / submodule updates could churn the fingerprint and cause spurious misses (re-execution). Mitigation: use stable markers (installed-lockfile content hash, `git submodule status` output, interpreter identity) — never mtimes or a full `node_modules` tree hash.
- **Sequencing with the audit-reuse items** — SA-0MWAXZHOU000UBG1 / SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI assume path-independent reuse; a coarse env fingerprint preserves that for equivalent environments but changes the lookup surface they build on. Mitigation: coordinate; land the fingerprint as backward-compatible (equiv-env sharing proven by tests) and cross-reference both items.
- **Escalation cost inside `finish`** — a forced run holds the exclusive main-checkout lock and competes for test slots. Mitigation: targeted `--scope changed --force` default; escalate to forced full only on broad/refactor/drift; reuse the existing paced/locked runner.
- **Dirty or locked main checkout at escalation** — the canonical checkout may not be runnable when the post-push step fires. Mitigation: documented, explicit degradation (never a silent green): report missing with a recovery recipe rather than accepting the drifted entry.
- **Scope creep** — this item must not grow into a general cache redesign (per-host caches, env pinning, cross-machine invalidation). Record such opportunities as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption** — `git submodule status` and the installed `node_modules` state are adequate coarse proxies for runtime environment; a submodule whose checkout is complete and `node_modules` whose resolution matches are equivalent for cache-reuse purposes.

## Related work

- SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN / SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG (completed) — tree-keyed gate verdicts and `fingerprint_kind="tree"`; the environment fingerprint extends this namespace.
- SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 (completed) — verdict provenance ("which tree ran, cached or executed"); the environment descriptor extends provenance.
- SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3 (pre-push cache mirroring, completed) — mirroring must become environment-aware.
- SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH (completed) — `--gate-commit` clean-checkout gate; unchanged, only entry bindability changes.
- SA-0MWAXZHOU000UBG1 / SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI (open) — audit tree-keyed cache reuse: their path-independent-reuse assumption must stay satisfiable for equivalent environments; coordinate sequencing.
- SA-0MVCF5SHU002WNYU (open) — pre-push bypass documentation; reconcile, do not duplicate.
- SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG (completed) — live-repo guard + push timeout; reconcile.

### Related work (automated find-related report, SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L)

- **SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN** (completed) — push to dev from the worktree that holds the commit: the worktree-push premise behind this item.
- **SA-0MSGNUXT3009LV7S** (completed) — wire cache into `run_tests.py`: the cache integration this item extends.
- **SA-0MW6VXSF8004X1PK** (completed) — [test-failure] "post-push full-suite verification: no valid full-suite cache entry": evidence of the verification's cache-miss/refusal behaviour this item refines.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which half (or both) should close the gap? (a) evidence policy only; (b) key integrity only; (c) both (provenance recorded and keyed, plus a forced targeted escalation when no canonical-environment entry exists)." — Answer (producer, rgardler): **"(c) Both"** (selected option letter c). Source: interactive reply on the work item (comment SA-C0MWFYLQ9A005IQWN, 2026-11-14).
- Q2: "What counts as environment identity if the key changes? (a) coarse, path-independent environment fingerprint (submodule completeness, node_modules resolution, interpreter); (b) full checkout identity (git common dir + worktree path); (c) provenance metadata only, key unchanged." — Answer (producer, rgardler): **"(a) coarse, path-independent environment fingerprint"**. Source: interactive reply (same comment thread).
- Q3: "Post-push behaviour when the only entry is drift-keyed? (a) escalate once, targeted (`--scope changed --force` in the canonical checkout; full force for broad/refactor/drift); (b) refuse the transition and recover manually; (c) accept with an `environment_drift` note." — Answer (producer, rgardler): **"(a) escalate once, targeted"**. Source: interactive reply (same comment thread).

All three answers arrived together as "1. c / 2. a / 3. a" in reply to the recorded question comment; the recommended options were adopted as chosen. Research summary (recorded in the question comment): post-push verification is read-only + tree-keyed today; pre-push runs the gate in a clean checkout (worktree in place) and mirrors entries into the main cache assuming content-address identity; the residual hazard is an environment-blind key (identical key ≠ identical runtime environment).
data.title: test-cache key ignores worktree/env identity: post-push verification can silently cache-serve

# plan-if-needed overwrites operator-confirmed effort/risk

Discovered-from: SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 (plan session 2026-10-27).

## Problem

`skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` `plan-if-needed` re-runs the effort-and-risk
estimator whenever no prior `effort_and_risk_skill` comment exists on the item
(`is_effort_risk_computed`), silently overwriting operator-confirmed
effort/risk values with heuristic estimates. On SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 the
operator-confirmed carry-over risk High / effort M was replaced with Extra
Small / Low (comment 09:38:39Z), materially understating risk of a commit-gate
change. The original values were restored manually.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plan-if-needed` never overwrites an explicitly set/human-confirmed
      effort or risk with a heuristic recomputation; the recompute path is gated
      on the absence of a deliberate value (with a recorded rationale), or the
      overwrite is surfaced as an explicit warning/approval.
- [ ] A regression test covers the overwrite scenario (operator value present,
      no prior estimator comment) and asserts the value is preserved.
- [ ] Origin case documented: SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 restore comment
      SA-C0MVQKM7XD0089OVQ.
data.title: plan-if-needed overwrites operator-confirmed effort/risk
